question: Should an AI system be allowed to make a diagnosis without a doctor signing it off?
sides: No, keep a doctor in the loop
answer: In several narrow tasks these systems already match specialists, and they do it at three in the morning in places with no specialist at all. Requiring a signature from someone who is not available is not a safety measure, it is a shortage dressed as one.
move: The real question is not accuracy on average. It is what happens on the case that falls outside the training data.
counterpoint: A doctor who signs off catches the case the model has never seen, and the model does not know which case that is. Add a rubber-stamping human and you get the worst of both: nobody actually checking, and nobody clearly responsible when it is wrong.
